newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco says optimistic will reach Sudbury deal.
newsitem.headline: Inco says optimistic will reach Sudbury deal.

text.p: Inco Ltd said on Friday it is optimistic a tentative agreement can be reached with unionized workers at its Sudbury, and Port Colborne, Ontario operations before the union's midnight May 31 strike deadline.
"We're still optimistic that we will have a new three-year contract by the end of the month," Inco spokesman Jerry Rogers told Reuters in a telephone interview from Sudbury.

Workers at Inco's Ontario operations on Thursday voted 98-percent in favor of giving union leaders a mandate to strike if a tentative agreement cannot be reached by midnight May 31, when the current contract expires.
The two sides have been negotiating for about three weeks. The current deal between Inco and 4,620 workers represented by the United Steelworkers of America expires May 31.
Rogers said the strike mandate was an expected development and he remained confident a deal could be reached.

"We're still optimistic. We're talking on a virtually daily basis. Last night they had a 98-percent vote in favor of a strike (mandate) but that doesn't come as a particular surprise because when they come back near the end of the month they have to come back to the membership anyway with something for a vote," Rogers said.
He declined to comment on specific aspects of the negotiations but said several issues remained outstanding.
"We're working with the union towards a successful win-win contract that's good for them and also strengthens the competitiveness of (Inco's) Ontario division," Rogers said.
The contract affects workers at the nickel giant's mining, smelting and refinery operations in Sudbury and its refinery in Port Colborne.
